transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we've had a strong quarter and the board finance committee has discussed a preliminary gross distribution of $3,000,000 as a one-time cash dividend to common shareholders. Before I finalize the distribution plan, I want to hear from each of you on the treasury, tax, and corporate-law side. Are there any items that could affect execution of this distribution? Please go ahead and share anything relevant.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important from the treasury side. This morning I confirmed in our 13-week cash forecast that treasury must retain exactly $2,100,000 of unrestricted cash after the distribution to cover scheduled debt service and payroll. The updated forecast has not yet been attached to the board file. With $5,000,000 in unrestricted cash and a $2,100,000 minimum retention requirement, that leaves only $2,900,000 available for distribution — which is $100,000 short of the preliminary $3,000,000 gross distribution figure.

First, we need to set aside a $180,000 withholding reserve for this distribution. Second, the payment date must be 2026-09-30 to align with our remittance schedule. I had not yet circulated this memo before this meeting.

While reviewing the charter this week, I found that the dividend requires a 2026-09-15 shareholder record date and a signed solvency certificate before payment. Neither of these requirements has been added to the distribution checklist yet. Circulate the tax memo to the distribution team and incorporate the $180,000 withholding reserve into the plan.
